tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

Injectable ultrasonic sensor for wireless
monitoring of intracranial signals

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07334-y

Received: 10 October 2023

Accepted: 19 March 2024

Published online: 5 June 2024

 Check for updates

Hanchuan Tang1,2,7, Yueying Yang1,7, Zhen Liu3,7, Wenlong Li4, Yipeng Zhang1, Yizhou Huang1,
Tianyu Kang1, Yang Yu1, Na Li1, Ye Tian1, Xurui Liu1, Yifan Cheng1, Zhouping Yin5,
Xiaobing Jiang3 ✉, Xiaodong Chen2 ✉ & Jianfeng Zang1,6 ✉

Direct and precise monitoring of intracranial physiology holds immense importance
in delineating injuries, prognostication and averting disease1. Wired clinical
instruments that use percutaneous leads are accurate but are susceptible to
infection, patient mobility constraints and potential surgical complications during
removal2. Wireless implantable devices provide greater operational freedom but
include issues such as limited detection range, poor degradation and difficulty in
size reduction in the human body3. Here we present an injectable, bioresorbable
and wireless metastructured hydrogel (metagel) sensor for ultrasonic monitoring
of intracranial signals. The metagel sensors are cubes 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 in size that
encompass both biodegradable and stimulus-responsive hydrogels and periodically
aligned air columns with a specific acoustic reflection spectrum. Implanted into
intracranial space with a puncture needle, the metagel deforms in response to
physiological environmental changes, causing peak frequency shifts of reflected
ultrasound waves that can be wirelessly measured by an external ultrasound probe.
The metagel sensor can independently detect intracranial pressure, temperature,
pH and flow rate, realize a detection depth of 10 cm and almost fully degrade within
18 weeks. Animal experiments on rats and pigs indicate promising multiparametric
sensing performances on a par with conventional non-resorbable wired clinical
benchmarks.

38: Wireless implantable sensors provide a promising solution for intrac-
39: ranial monitoring in comparison with traditional clinical instruments4.
40: Current wireless implantable sensors, mainly using near-field commu-
41: nication5–10, inductive coupling11–15 or ultrasonic communication16–21,
42: have been developed for monitoring of parameters in the human body,
43: including pressure, flow rate, temperature and pH. Nevertheless, sev-
44: eral inter-related challenges pertaining to current wireless implantable
45: sensors hinder their clinical applications, including implant size, com-
46: munication range and stability, biocompatibility and bioresorbability,
47: and multimodal sensing and decoupling.
48: 
49: In regard to intracranial devices, optimal implant sizes (for example,
50: cross-sectional area less than approximately 4 mm2) are desired to
51: permit injection into the brain via minimally invasive puncture nee-
52: dles22. Full biodegradability of implants negates the requirement for
53: additional surgical removal procedures. Communication distance is
54: inherently linked to the depth within the body at which signals can
55: be detected (for example, subdural or brain ventricular). Simultane-
56: ously, the sensing system must counteract signal interferences from
57: physiological surroundings. Moreover, achieving multimodal and
58: decoupled physiological signals is necessary for an intricate and
59: 
60: precise depiction of bodily health. Despite substantial efforts, current
61: electronics-based research manages to tackle only a subset of these
62: challenges3.

64: Soft acoustic metamaterials possess extraordinary acoustic proper-
65: ties for long-distance wireless sensing and communication without
66: the addition of electronic components23–26. We hypothesize that soft
67: acoustic metamaterials incorporating hydrogel as base material27,28
68: and a wearable ultrasound device29–32 as wireless readers can address
69: the comprehensive challenges posed by wireless implantable sensors.

391: Fig. 1 | Design of injectable and biodegradable metagel ultrasonic sensor.
392: a, Diagram showing metagels as wireless intracranial physiology sensors using
393: ultrasound reflection. b, Photograph of metagel samples and puncture needle
394: for delivery. c, Microscopy image showing metagel structure. d, Photographs
395: showing a metagel degrading following 1 month in PBS solution at 37 °C; dashed
396: line delineates the shape of the metagel. e, Diagram illustrating the working
397: 
398: principle of metagels based on environment-induced microdeformation.
399: f, Schematic showing peak frequency shifts of metagel due to deformation.
400: g, Energy band structures of metagel. h,i, Calculated bandgap central frequency
401: dependence on lattice constants a (h) and filling ratio d/a (i). j,k, Simulated
402: sound scatter field of metagels before ( j) and after (k) deformation. Scale bars,
403: 2 mm (b), 500 μm (c). a.u., arbitrary units.
404: 
405: Design of metagel ultrasonic sensor
406: The metagel senses intracranial environment based on environment-
407: induced microdeformation. It includes a hydrogel matrix and periodic
408: air columns, forming a soft phononic crystal33 with adjustable acoustic
409: reflection spectra (Fig. 1e). This structural design imparts exceptional
410: acoustic reflective properties to the metagel. When emitted by ultra-
411: sound waves (with peak frequency f0) the metagel reflects these at a
412: peak frequency of f1. Intracranial environmental change induces micro-
413: deformation of the metagel, changing the reflected peak frequency
414: (f1 + Δf). With stimulus-responsive functionalization on the hydrogel
415: 
416: matrix (pressure-, temperature-, pH-responsive and so on), the metagel
417: can track environmental change by tracing the peak frequency shift of
418: reflected ultrasound waves (Fig. 1f).
419: 
420: To understand how the metagel design affects ultrasound reflec-
421: tiveness, we calculated its band structures. With a lattice constant a
422: and filler diameter d, the bandgaps of metagel can be calculated by
423: solving the eigenvalue equations of a single cell with Bloch bounda-
424: ries. With a = 0.28 mm and d = 0.196 mm, the metagel features acous-
425: tic bandgaps centred at 8.2  and 9.2 MHz (Fig. 1g). When ultrasound
426: waves with frequencies falling within these bandgaps transmit to the
427: metagel, most energy will be reflected, rendering the metagel readily
428: 
429: Nature  |  Vol 630  |  6 June 2024  |  85
430: 
431:  distinguishable through ultrasound imaging. The bandgaps of metagel
432: are dependent on a and filling ratio (FR = d/a) (Fig. 1h,i, Supplementary
433: Figs. 3 and 4 and Supplementary Note 2). Thus, metagel deformation
434: causing changes in a and FR exhibits bandgap changes (Supplemen-
435: tary Fig. 5). Finite-element simulation of sound field can indicate the
436: reflected peak frequency shift due to metagel deformation. The peak
437: frequency of sound waves reflected by the undeformed metagel is about
438: 9.13 MHz (Fig. 1j), agreeing with the bandgap calculation in Fig. 1g. As
439: the metagel undergoes deformation due to changes in the physiological
440: environment, the peak frequency of reflected waves shifts to 9.76 MHz
441: (Fig. 1k). Further simulations investigating the influence of metagel
442: designs can be found in Supplementary Figs. 6–10 and Supplementary
443: Note 3. The operational mechanism of metagel-based ultrasonic sens-
444: ing is also delineated in Supplementary Video 1.
445: 
446: Characterization of the ultrasonic sensor
447: The metagel matrix used to detect pressure changes is a tough and
448: stimulus-inert hydrogel composed of a polyvinyl alcohol/carboxyme-
449: thyl chitosan (PVA/CMC) double network. External pressure compresses
450: the air column within the metagel, leading to an increase in ultrasound
451: reflection peak frequency. A stimulus-responsive component incorpo-
452: rated in the hydrogel matrix endures the ability of the metagel to sense
453: other signals. Specifically, a PVA/poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PVA/
454: PNIPAM) double-network hydrogel was engineered to sense tempera-
455: ture changes and a PVA/chitosan (CS) double-network hydrogel was
456: devised to detect shifts in pH (Fig. 2a). The mechanical and responsive
457: properties of the metagels are characterized and simulated in Sup-
458: plementary Figs. 11–14 and Extended Data Fig. 2.
459: 
460: Figure 2b illustrates the shape of a metagel and a pure hydrogel
461: under ultrasound imaging. The metagel shows clear signals, whereas
462: the pure hydrogel is nearly transparent. The echo intensities received
463: by the ultrasonic probe and related fast Fourier transform spectra
464: are outlined in Fig. 2c,d, indicating a 50-fold enhancement in echoes
465: from the metagel in comparison with pure hydrogel. Further com-
466: parisons of ultrasonic characteristics between metagel and common
467: biological tissues are depicted in Supplementary Figs. 15 and 16 and
468: Supplementary Note 5.
469: 
470: Based on our proposed metagel ultrasonic sensing system, multiple
471: signals can be monitored. The workflow of metagel ultrasonic sensing
472: involves the injection of metagels, affixing ultrasound devices onto
473: the skin, B-mode imaging, determining the incident angle, initiating
474: ultrasonic emission and reception and processing received signals
475: (Extended Data Fig. 3). Further details about this workflow and inci-
476: dent angle determination are given in Supplementary Figs. 17–20 and
477: Supplementary Note 6. In vitro experiments were conducted to meas-
478: ure pressure, temperature, pH and flow rate. Specifically, the range,
479: resolution and stability of the pressure metagel sensor were evalu-
480: ated, as shown in Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 4a–f. The metagel can
481: effectively measure pressure changes in the range 0–70 mmHg with
482: a resolution of 0.1 mmHg and sensitivity of 5.7 kHz mmHg−1 (Fig. 2f).
483: Real-time pressure measurements using the metagel and commercial
484: manometer are demonstrated in Supplementary Video 2. In addition,
485: temperature metagels were tested in customized set-ups, as illustrated
486: in Fig. 2g. The results demonstrate the correspondence between fre-
487: quency and temperature of the metagel across a broad temperature
488: range spanning 28–43 °C, covering core temperature variation in the
489: human body. The temperature metagel exhibits a resolution of 0.1 °C
490: and sensitivity of approximately 80 kHz °C−1 (Fig. 2h and Extended Data
491: Fig. 4g–l). pH metagels were designed to detect pH changes from 8.0
492: to 2.0, as illustrated in Fig. 2i. Detailed experiments on pH variations
493: indicate that a pH change as small as 0.5 can be detected. Based on a
494: sensitivity of 256.4 kHz per pH unit, it is possible to discern pH changes
495: as minute as 0.0012 (Fig. 2j and Supplementary Figs. 22 and 23). Sup-
496: plementary Video 3 shows the morphological changes of metagels in
497: 
498: 86  |  Nature  |  Vol 630  |  6 June 2024
499: 
500: response to varying environmental temperature and pH conditions.
501: In addition, the pressure metagel can also detect the flow rate of brain
502: vascular vessels when positioned in close proximity. In a brain tissue
503: model, pulsed fluid flow causes vibrations in the metagel; the envelope
504: of the received signals reflects the flow rate of the vessel (Fig. 2k and
505: Supplementary Fig. 24), agreeing well with results for a commercial flow
506: sensor. Metagel injection and dynamic flow measurement are detailed
507: in Supplementary Videos 4 and 5. Furthermore, metagel sensors dem-
508: onstrated robust ultrasound performance under fatigue testing with
509: 2,600 pressurization cycles (Extended Data Fig. 5, Supplementary
510: Fig. 25 and Supplementary Note 12), indicating their operational sta-
511: bility for real applications.
512: 
513: As a multiparametric sensing system, the decoupling of each distinct
514: signal is crucial for accurate clinical monitoring. Indeed, disentangling
515: the desired signal from diverse environmental interferences, especially
516: in the realm of wireless sensors, remains a formidable challenge. In this
517: context we present a decoupling approach centred on simultaneous
518: monitoring of multiple metagels. The pulse repetition frequency of
519: the ultrasonic probe can reach 10 kHz, permitting cyclic sequential
520: scanning of diverse metagels with time intervals as short as 0.1 ms; envi-
521: ronmental changes in the body can be assumed negligible within such a
522: compact time frame. Moreover, the impressive spatial resolution of the
523: ultrasound probe allows differentiation of two closely situated metagels
524: (with a minimum separation of 1 mm; Supplementary Fig. 26). Guided
525: by this approach, the concurrent assessment of response attributes for
526: three metagels under a particular single environmental factor becomes
527: possible (Extended Data Fig. 6). We found that pressure substantially
528: affects all three metagels, whereas the influence of either temperature
529: or pH is markedly pronounced only on the temperature metagel and
530: pH metagel, respectively. We also investigated the combined influence
531: of two environmental factors (pressure and temperature, pressure and
532: pH) on the three metagels (Extended Data Fig. 7, Supplementary Fig. 27
533: and Supplementary Note 13). The effects of environmental factors
534: appear to be independent and nearly linear across the targeted measur-
535: ing range, permitting the decoupling of these factors by simultaneous
536: measurement of two metagels (Extended Data Fig. 7d).
537: 
538: The metagel ultrasonic sensing system also shows long communica-
539: tion distance and reduced heat generation. Due to the robust sound
540: reflection attributes of metagels and facile tissue penetration of ultra-
541: sound, the communication distance between metagels and ultrasound
542: probe can be greater than 10 cm (Supplementary Fig. 29), allowing
543: thorough detection of brain tissue. The system generates minimal heat,
544: with tissue temperature remaining at 22 °C over 60 min of ultrasound
545: sensing and thereby ensuring safety for human application (Supple-
546: mentary Fig. 30). We also analysed the impact of the ultrasound system
547: configuration and the processing of the acquired raw time-domain data
548: on outcomes (Supplementary Figs. 31–33 and Supplementary Note 15),
549: and discuss the metagel ultrasonic sensing performance in terms of
550: detection limits, sensing range and time resolution (Supplementary
551: Fig. 34 and Supplementary Note 16).
552: 
553: In vivo animal sensing
554: We first evaluated in vivo sensing performance using a rat model. Before
555: animal experiments we conducted in vitro cell culture tests to verify
556: the biocompatibility of the metagel, confirming the non-toxic nature
557: of all three types (Supplementary Fig. 35). The metagel was delivered
558: 5 mm beneath the rat skull using a puncture needle (Supplementary
559: Video 6). For comparison, a clinically used wired intracranial pressure
560: (ICP) probe (fibre-optic pressure sensing, Codman) was simultane-
561: ously implanted (Fig. 3a). Notably, drilling of the skull is necessary for
562: both clinical ICP sensing and metagel implantation. The hole (typically
563: 5.8 mm in diameter) left in the skull following drilling serves conveni-
564: ently as a window for ultrasound propagation. Further discussion on
565: the acoustic window is shown in Supplementary Note 18.

1187: Representative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) shows the loca-
1188: tion of the implanted metagel inside the live rat’s skull (Fig. 3b and
1189: Supplementary Fig. 36), confirming that it can be clearly visualized
1190: using MRI without inducing any artefacts. We also investigated the
1191: implanted metagel under microcomputed tomography (Supplemen-
1192: tary Fig. 37); as with soft tissues, metagel appears transparent and
1193: showed no disruption in these microcomputed tomography images.
1194: Following metagel implantation, an ultrasound probe with an adhesive
1195: encapsulating layer can be affixed in the rat to monitor intracranial
1196: physiological parameters (Fig. 3c). Notably, there is no percutaneous
1197: lead between the metagel and ultrasound probe, distinguishing it from
1198: wired clinical ICP probes.

1200: For monitoring of intracranial pressure, periodic compression of
1201: the rat abdomen (flank squeeze manoeuvre) was performed, induc-
1202: ing changes in intracranial pressure that were effectively tracked by
1203: both the pressure metagel and clinical ICP probe. The waveforms indi-
1204: cated that the metagel outperformed the clinical ICP probe in terms
1205: of pressure resolution and time accuracy (Fig. 3d). For intracranial
1206: 
1207: temperature monitoring, intracranial temperature was adjusted by
1208: positioning a heating blanket or an ice pack close to the rat brain. A
1209: commercially available wired temperature probe was also inserted
1210: intracranially for comparison. The temperature metagel registered
1211: temperature changes akin to the commercial probe (Fig. 3e,f), the
1212: results indicating reduced core body temperature in the anaesthetized
1213: rat model. Furthermore, we documented the long-term intracranial
1214: pressure sensing performance of metagel in the rat (Fig. 3g). Over four
1215: samplings spanning 24 days from implantation, intracranial measure-
1216: ments by the metagel closely aligned with those of the clinical ICP,
1217: signifying the ability of the former to maintain intracranial stability
1218: over 24 days. In addition we also detected traumatic brain injury in
1219: the rat using metagels, providing further insight into its potential for
1220: clinical application (Supplementary Fig. 38).

Direct and precise monitoring of intracranial physiology holds immense importance
in delineating injuries, prognostication and averting disease1. Wired clinical
instruments that use percutaneous leads are accurate but are susceptible to
infection, patient mobility constraints and potential surgical complications during
removal2. Wireless implantable devices provide greater operational freedom but
include issues such as limited detection range, poor degradation and difficulty in
size reduction in the human body3. Here we present an injectable, bioresorbable
and wireless metastructured hydrogel (metagel) sensor for ultrasonic monitoring
of intracranial signals. The metagel sensors are cubes 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 in size that
encompass both biodegradable and stimulus-responsive hydrogels and periodically
aligned air columns with a specific acoustic reflection spectrum. Implanted into
intracranial space with a puncture needle, the metagel deforms in response to
physiological environmental changes, causing peak frequency shifts of reflected
ultrasound waves that can be wirelessly measured by an external ultrasound probe.
The metagel sensor can independently detect intracranial pressure, temperature,
pH and flow rate, realize a detection depth of 10 cm and almost fully degrade within
18 weeks. Animal experiments on rats and pigs indicate promising multiparametric
sensing performances on a par with conventional non-resorbable wired clinical
Wireless implantable sensors provide a promising solution for intrac-
ranial monitoring in comparison with traditional clinical instruments4.
Current wireless implantable sensors, mainly using near-field commu-
nication5–10, inductive coupling11–15 or ultrasonic communication16–21,
have been developed for monitoring of parameters in the human body,
including pressure, flow rate, temperature and pH. Nevertheless, sev-
eral inter-related challenges pertaining to current wireless implantable
sensors hinder their clinical applications, including implant size, com-
munication range and stability, biocompatibility and bioresorbability,
In regard to intracranial devices, optimal implant sizes (for example,
cross-sectional area less than approximately 4 mm2) are desired to
permit injection into the brain via minimally invasive puncture nee-
dles22. Full biodegradability of implants negates the requirement for
additional surgical removal procedures. Communication distance is
inherently linked to the depth within the body at which signals can
be detected (for example, subdural or brain ventricular). Simultane-
ously, the sensing system must counteract signal interferences from
physiological surroundings. Moreover, achieving multimodal and
decoupled physiological signals is necessary for an intricate and
precise depiction of bodily health. Despite substantial efforts, current
electronics-based research manages to tackle only a subset of these
Soft acoustic metamaterials possess extraordinary acoustic proper-
ties for long-distance wireless sensing and communication without
the addition of electronic components23–26. We hypothesize that soft
acoustic metamaterials incorporating hydrogel as base material27,28
and a wearable ultrasound device29–32 as wireless readers can address
the comprehensive challenges posed by wireless implantable sensors.
In this work we present a new paradigm for metagel ultrasonic sens-
ing. With a soft acoustic metamaterial, a fully bioresorbable and min-
iaturized metastructured hydrogel (metagel). as the only implant,
rich intracranial physiological signals (pressure, temperature, pH
and flow rate) can be wirelessly monitored using external ultrasonic
probes (Fig. 1a). The metagel, configured as a 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 cube, is
readily inserted into the body using a conventional puncture needle
(Fig. 1b,c). After the intended monitoring period (for example, 1 month),
the metagel naturally degrades win the PBS solution at 37 °C within
4 months (Fig. 1d, Extended Data Fig. 1, Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2

The metagel senses intracranial environment based on environment-
induced microdeformation. It includes a hydrogel matrix and periodic
air columns, forming a soft phononic crystal33 with adjustable acoustic
reflection spectra (Fig. 1e). This structural design imparts exceptional
acoustic reflective properties to the metagel. When emitted by ultra-
sound waves (with peak frequency f0) the metagel reflects these at a
peak frequency of f1. Intracranial environmental change induces micro-
deformation of the metagel, changing the reflected peak frequency
(f1 + Δf). With stimulus-responsive functionalization on the hydrogel
matrix (pressure-, temperature-, pH-responsive and so on), the metagel
can track environmental change by tracing the peak frequency shift of
To understand how the metagel design affects ultrasound reflec-
tiveness, we calculated its band structures. With a lattice constant a
and filler diameter d, the bandgaps of metagel can be calculated by
solving the eigenvalue equations of a single cell with Bloch bounda-
ries. With a = 0.28 mm and d = 0.196 mm, the metagel features acous-
tic bandgaps centred at 8.2  and 9.2 MHz (Fig. 1g). When ultrasound
waves with frequencies falling within these bandgaps transmit to the
metagel, most energy will be reflected, rendering the metagel readily
distinguishable through ultrasound imaging. The bandgaps of metagel
are dependent on a and filling ratio (FR = d/a) (Fig. 1h,i, Supplementary
Figs. 3 and 4 and Supplementary Note 2). Thus, metagel deformation
causing changes in a and FR exhibits bandgap changes (Supplemen-
tary Fig. 5). Finite-element simulation of sound field can indicate the
reflected peak frequency shift due to metagel deformation. The peak
frequency of sound waves reflected by the undeformed metagel is about
9.13 MHz (Fig. 1j), agreeing with the bandgap calculation in Fig. 1g. As
the metagel undergoes deformation due to changes in the physiological
environment, the peak frequency of reflected waves shifts to 9.76 MHz
(Fig. 1k). Further simulations investigating the influence of metagel
designs can be found in Supplementary Figs. 6–10 and Supplementary
Note 3. The operational mechanism of metagel-based ultrasonic sens-
ing is also delineated in Supplementary Video 1.
The metagel matrix used to detect pressure changes is a tough and
stimulus-inert hydrogel composed of a polyvinyl alcohol/carboxyme-
thyl chitosan (PVA/CMC) double network. External pressure compresses
the air column within the metagel, leading to an increase in ultrasound
reflection peak frequency. A stimulus-responsive component incorpo-
rated in the hydrogel matrix endures the ability of the metagel to sense

ture changes and a PVA/chitosan (CS) double-network hydrogel was
devised to detect shifts in pH (Fig. 2a). The mechanical and responsive
properties of the metagels are characterized and simulated in Sup-
plementary Figs. 11–14 and Extended Data Fig. 2.
Figure 2b illustrates the shape of a metagel and a pure hydrogel
under ultrasound imaging. The metagel shows clear signals, whereas
the pure hydrogel is nearly transparent. The echo intensities received
by the ultrasonic probe and related fast Fourier transform spectra
are outlined in Fig. 2c,d, indicating a 50-fold enhancement in echoes
from the metagel in comparison with pure hydrogel. Further com-

Based on our proposed metagel ultrasonic sensing system, multiple
signals can be monitored. The workflow of metagel ultrasonic sensing
involves the injection of metagels, affixing ultrasound devices onto
the skin, B-mode imaging, determining the incident angle, initiating
ultrasonic emission and reception and processing received signals
(Extended Data Fig. 3). Further details about this workflow and inci-
dent angle determination are given in Supplementary Figs. 17–20 and
Supplementary Note 6. In vitro experiments were conducted to meas-
ure pressure, temperature, pH and flow rate. Specifically, the range,
resolution and stability of the pressure metagel sensor were evalu-
ated, as shown in Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 4a–f. The metagel can
effectively measure pressure changes in the range 0–70 mmHg with
a resolution of 0.1 mmHg and sensitivity of 5.7 kHz mmHg−1 (Fig. 2f).
Real-time pressure measurements using the metagel and commercial
manometer are demonstrated in Supplementary Video 2. In addition,
temperature metagels were tested in customized set-ups, as illustrated
in Fig. 2g. The results demonstrate the correspondence between fre-
quency and temperature of the metagel across a broad temperature
range spanning 28–43 °C, covering core temperature variation in the
human body. The temperature metagel exhibits a resolution of 0.1 °C
and sensitivity of approximately 80 kHz °C−1 (Fig. 2h and Extended Data
Fig. 4g–l). pH metagels were designed to detect pH changes from 8.0
to 2.0, as illustrated in Fig. 2i. Detailed experiments on pH variations
indicate that a pH change as small as 0.5 can be detected. Based on a
sensitivity of 256.4 kHz per pH unit, it is possible to discern pH changes
as minute as 0.0012 (Fig. 2j and Supplementary Figs. 22 and 23). Sup-
plementary Video 3 shows the morphological changes of metagels in
response to varying environmental temperature and pH conditions.
In addition, the pressure metagel can also detect the flow rate of brain
vascular vessels when positioned in close proximity. In a brain tissue
model, pulsed fluid flow causes vibrations in the metagel; the envelope
of the received signals reflects the flow rate of the vessel (Fig. 2k and
Supplementary Fig. 24), agreeing well with results for a commercial flow
sensor. Metagel injection and dynamic flow measurement are detailed
in Supplementary Videos 4 and 5. Furthermore, metagel sensors dem-
onstrated robust ultrasound performance under fatigue testing with
Fig. 25 and Supplementary Note 12), indicating their operational sta-
As a multiparametric sensing system, the decoupling of each distinct
signal is crucial for accurate clinical monitoring. Indeed, disentangling
the desired signal from diverse environmental interferences, especially
in the realm of wireless sensors, remains a formidable challenge. In this
context we present a decoupling approach centred on simultaneous
monitoring of multiple metagels. The pulse repetition frequency of
the ultrasonic probe can reach 10 kHz, permitting cyclic sequential
scanning of diverse metagels with time intervals as short as 0.1 ms; envi-
ronmental changes in the body can be assumed negligible within such a
compact time frame. Moreover, the impressive spatial resolution of the
ultrasound probe allows differentiation of two closely situated metagels
(with a minimum separation of 1 mm; Supplementary Fig. 26). Guided
by this approach, the concurrent assessment of response attributes for
three metagels under a particular single environmental factor becomes
possible (Extended Data Fig. 6). We found that pressure substantially
affects all three metagels, whereas the influence of either temperature
or pH is markedly pronounced only on the temperature metagel and
pH metagel, respectively. We also investigated the combined influence
of two environmental factors (pressure and temperature, pressure and
pH) on the three metagels (Extended Data Fig. 7, Supplementary Fig. 27
and Supplementary Note 13). The effects of environmental factors
appear to be independent and nearly linear across the targeted measur-
ing range, permitting the decoupling of these factors by simultaneous
measurement of two metagels (Extended Data Fig. 7d).
The metagel ultrasonic sensing system also shows long communica-
tion distance and reduced heat generation. Due to the robust sound
reflection attributes of metagels and facile tissue penetration of ultra-
sound, the communication distance between metagels and ultrasound
probe can be greater than 10 cm (Supplementary Fig. 29), allowing
thorough detection of brain tissue. The system generates minimal heat,
with tissue temperature remaining at 22 °C over 60 min of ultrasound
sensing and thereby ensuring safety for human application (Supple-
mentary Fig. 30). We also analysed the impact of the ultrasound system
configuration and the processing of the acquired raw time-domain data
on outcomes (Supplementary Figs. 31–33 and Supplementary Note 15),
and discuss the metagel ultrasonic sensing performance in terms of
detection limits, sensing range and time resolution (Supplementary
We first evaluated in vivo sensing performance using a rat model. Before
animal experiments we conducted in vitro cell culture tests to verify
the biocompatibility of the metagel, confirming the non-toxic nature
of all three types (Supplementary Fig. 35). The metagel was delivered
5 mm beneath the rat skull using a puncture needle (Supplementary
Video 6). For comparison, a clinically used wired intracranial pressure
(ICP) probe (fibre-optic pressure sensing, Codman) was simultane-
ously implanted (Fig. 3a). Notably, drilling of the skull is necessary for
both clinical ICP sensing and metagel implantation. The hole (typically
5.8 mm in diameter) left in the skull following drilling serves conveni-
ently as a window for ultrasound propagation. Further discussion on
the acoustic window is shown in Supplementary Note 18.

Following metagel implantation, an ultrasound probe with an adhesive
encapsulating layer can be affixed in the rat to monitor intracranial
physiological parameters (Fig. 3c). Notably, there is no percutaneous
lead between the metagel and ultrasound probe, distinguishing it from
For monitoring of intracranial pressure, periodic compression of
the rat abdomen (flank squeeze manoeuvre) was performed, induc-
ing changes in intracranial pressure that were effectively tracked by
both the pressure metagel and clinical ICP probe. The waveforms indi-
cated that the metagel outperformed the clinical ICP probe in terms
of pressure resolution and time accuracy (Fig. 3d). For intracranial
temperature monitoring, intracranial temperature was adjusted by
positioning a heating blanket or an ice pack close to the rat brain. A
commercially available wired temperature probe was also inserted
intracranially for comparison. The temperature metagel registered
temperature changes akin to the commercial probe (Fig. 3e,f), the
results indicating reduced core body temperature in the anaesthetized
rat model. Furthermore, we documented the long-term intracranial
pressure sensing performance of metagel in the rat (Fig. 3g). Over four

课题「电化学传感」（dqb-project）核心记忆 v4：

# 课题核心记忆：基于电化学平台技术课题设想（dqb-project）

> 归档说明：本版由《课题汇报.pptx》（2026/08/15，邓启彬，26 页）整理归档而来（v1 占位内容更新）；v3 新增 MMBC 对标文献精读卡归档与「8 指标同步」表述澄清；v4 新增 Adv. Mater. 2025 纤维可植入探针综述精读总结归档（与课题一介入导管强相关）。
> 详细总结见 `archive/2026-08-15_基于电化学平台技术课题设想_课题设计总结.md`，原始 PPT 见 `archive/原始材料/`。

## 1. 课题身份与定位

- 负责人：邓启彬；课题框架：**基于电化学平台技术的两个课题设想**（2026/08/15 汇报）。
- 依托技术积累：
  - 介入导丝项目：微型导丝内部电极集成、导丝运动控制；
  - 电化学传感通用平台：电极修饰研究、电化学前端电路及软件开发；
  - 苏大电致变色组件合作：连续多指标原位传感器（肾内科应用）。
- 个人专业背景支撑：电路 / 软件 / 结构设计可满足组内需求。

## 2. 课题一：术中监测介入导管

- **临床痛点**：术中血气分析依赖间歇采血 + 离体检测，①有数分钟等待时间；②只能评价全身指标，无法判断介入位置微环境（病灶局部 pH、氧分压、乳酸梯度被血流稀释）。
- **方案**：尺寸与功能不变的介入导管侧壁内集成 4 个线控单元调节头端方向 + 头端集成多个工作电极，术中原位多生化指标传感。
- **创新点**：①操控与传感一体化（四向牵引丝 + 电极阵列共集成）；②靶区多指标实时监测（多工作电极 + 共享参比/对电极）；③"导管导航—靶区感知—术中决策"闭环（病变区 vs 正常组织多指标差异 → 定位/边界/消融给药依据）。
- **对标文献**：MMBC 磁控导管（Nat. Mater. 24, 2019–2031 (2025)，DOI: 10.1038/s41563-025-02340-5；中山大学谢曦/蒋乐伦团队；**8 指标多参数能力**——代谢物（Crea/UA/H₂O₂/Ep）与离子（K⁺/Na⁺/Ca²⁺/pH）两套微电极，体内分场景测量，非同一时刻全同步；兔 ARF + 猪血管介入验证）；MDMOC 磁性光电导管（Nat. Commun. 17, 3725 (2026)，Φ2.5 mm，肿瘤边界 pH/H₂O₂/K⁺/GSH 测绘）；纤维可植入探针综述（Adv. Mater. 2025, 2504372，DOI: 10.1002/adma.202504372，北大邵元龙组，见 §6 精读总结）。
- **主要风险**：0.15–0.20 mm 薄壁内线控+电极集成工艺；电极长期稳定（酶/离子膜易失活漂移，MIP 不能连续测量）；需专业大动物实验资源。

## 3. 课题二：连续可视化传感贴片（肾内科合作）

- **临床痛点**：维持性血液透析患者（每周 2–3 次）48–72 h 透析间期溶质/电解质/容量负荷无患者侧连续监测；较长透析间期后死亡及心血管住院事件率升高（NEJM 365, 1099–1107 (2011)）。
- **方案（四层结构）**：组织液电极细丝（K⁺ 为主、尿素/肌酐为辅）→ 贴片连接层（固定+贴肤）→ 电化学前端电路（信号→浓度→电平）→ 电致变色控制层（按浓度显示条带宽度，原位显示）。
- **创新点**：①完整透析周期连续监测；②可穿戴全功能链集成；③直观且安全的患者反馈。
- **优先监测指标**：尿素、肌酐、K⁺、PO₄³⁻、尿酸、β₂-微球蛋白、硫酸吲哚酚、对甲酚硫酸盐。
- **对标文献**：可拉伸表皮汗液电致变色贴片（Nat. Electron. 5, 694–705 (2022)，Joseph Wang 组，丝网印刷）；无电池可原位再生汗液贴片（Nat. Biomed. Eng. (2026)，Rahim Esfandyarpour 组，PPy/o-PD MIP + 普鲁士蓝，原位再生率约 98.7%，21 天验证）。
- **主要风险**：前端小型柔性化（小信号干扰、阻抗匹配）；电极耐久一致性；组织液电极—前端—电致变色整链集成与贴敷稳定性。

## 4. 共同技术问题：电化学电极修饰

- 七条路线对比结论：**酶电极与离子选择电极成熟度最高；适配体电极创新潜力最大；免疫、MIP、核酸电极更适合间歇/一次性检测**（详细对比表见归档总结 §3.1）。
- 三条重点修饰体系（PPT 详解）：
  1. **MIP 分子印迹电极**：肌酐模板 + 丙烯酸甲酯功能单体 + EGDMA 交联网络；聚合包埋→洗脱模板→重结合读出；风险=模板残留、传质慢。
  2. **离子选择电极**：PVC/DOS/缬氨霉素选择膜 + PEDOT:PSS 固体接触层；E = E⁰ + (RT/F)ln a(K⁺)；风险=参比漂移、膜组分浸出。
  3. **功能高分子修饰**：PDA（黏附固定）+ PSBMA（水化抗污）+ PEDOT:PSS（导电增敏）；风险=膜厚传质、批差。
- **共同瓶颈**：长期稳定的电化学修饰电极（两课题共享，优先攻关方向）。

## 5. 关键文献（PPT 编号 + 后续归档文献）

| [8] | Nat. Biomed. Eng. (2026) | 课题二：可再生汗液贴片 |
| [9] | Adv. Mater. 2025, 2504372；DOI: 10.1002/adma.202504372 | 课题一技术对标综述：生物材料基纤维可植入探针（纤维制备/表面修饰/生化传感/封装，精读总结已入库，见 §6） |

<skill_instructions>
# Nature Paper Card - Router

Use this skill to turn one paper into an evidence-grounded research card, not a translated abstract, generic summary, reviewer report, or publication article.

The skill uses:

- a static core under `static/core/` for principles, workflow, and the fixed output contract;
- one paper-type fragment under `static/fragments/paper_type/`;
- on-demand references for evidence labels, the exact card schema, and research-idea checks.

## Routing protocol

Follow these steps every time.

### 1. Load the manifest and core layer

Read [manifest.yaml](manifest.yaml), then read every file under `always_load`. Do not generate the card from this router alone.

### 2. Establish the source boundary

Identify which material is available:

- full paper with figures and tables;
- paper text without reliable layout;
- abstract or metadata only;
- an existing `nature-reader` artifact with stable source IDs.

Prefer an existing `nature-reader` artifact when supplied. Do not repeat full bilingual translation or figure extraction. If only partial material is available, create a visibly partial card and mark every unsupported section `Not assessable from supplied material`.

For a PDF or `nature-reader` source-map JSON, the bundled script is mandatory.

1. Resolve `SKILL_DIR` as the directory containing this loaded `SKILL.md`.
2. Verify `SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_paper.py` exists.
3. Run exactly the bundled script by its resolved path:

```text
python "SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_paper.py" INPUT \
  --output WORKDIR/source_bundle.json
```

Add `--render-dir WORKDIR/rendered-pages` when visual page review is needed. Inspect the script exit code and the bundle validation block before drafting.

For source-map input, also inspect `locator_summary` and `unlocated_blocks`. Only records under `pages` have verified positive PDF page locators. Missing or invalid page locators remain in `unlocated_blocks` with an explicit status and must be cited structurally, never as page 1.

Never write inline Python, a temporary extraction script, or a replacement script during a Paper Card run. Never patch the bundled scripts during a normal Paper Card run. Modify these scripts only when the user explicitly asks to develop, debug, or improve the skill itself.

Use this fixed locator state machine:

- `page-grounded`: the bundled script succeeds and validates reliable PDF page indices. Use PDF page plus structural locators. Printed page labels are optional metadata.
- `structure-grounded`: page extraction is unreliable, but reliable sections, figures, tables, equations, source blocks, or full text remain available. Do not emit page-number citations.
- `source-limited`: only an abstract, metadata, or user-provided excerpt is reliable. Do not emit page-number citations or infer unseen evidence.

If preparation fails, record the failure. Prefer an existing `nature-reader` source map or the environment PDF/OCR capability, but do not create a replacement script. Then enter the strongest supported fallback mode.

### 3. Classify the paper type

Use the manifest to choose one primary `paper_type` and, only for a genuinely hybrid paper, one secondary contribution lens:

- `methods`
- `discovery`
- `resource`
- `clinical`
- `materials`
- `review`

Load the primary fragment and no more than one secondary fragment. Classify by the paper's argument and evidence structure, not merely its discipline. State both selections before analysis. For example, an algorithm paper that also introduces a substantial dataset may use `methods` as the primary lens and `resource` as the secondary lens.

### 4. Build the evidence base before drafting

Build an internal evidence inventory before drafting. At minimum, enumerate:

- bibliographic metadata and access status;
- research question and claimed contribution;
- method components, assumptions, and data flow;
- every main figure, table, and essential equation with its argumentative role;
- experiments, baselines, metrics, ablations, and reported results;
- author-stated limitations;
- stable source pointers to pages, sections, equations, figures, tables, or `nature-reader` block IDs.

Then build a compact claim-evidence matrix linking each central claim to the evidence that supports it and to any unresolved gap.

Use external search only for Section 04, Section 15, bibliographic verification, or an explicit novelty check. Never present the paper's own related-work narrative as independently verified field history. Record whether the context mode is `paper-only`, `targeted external check`, or `externally verified`.

### 5. Generate the fixed Sections 01-16 Paper Card

Apply, in order:

1. core principles;
2. the selected paper-type fragment;
3. core workflow;
4. output contract.

Read [references/evidence-and-provenance.md](references/evidence-and-provenance.md) before making analytical or externally verified claims. Read [references/card-schema.md](references/card-schema.md) when drafting the final Markdown. Read [references/research-idea-gates.md](references/research-idea-gates.md) before writing Section 16.

Write a real Markdown artifact, defaulting to `paper-card.md`. Keep all 16 numbered sections in order, but write `Not applicable` or `Not assessable` instead of inventing content.

Match the user's language by default. The skill source and schema remain English, but localize the Paper Card headings and prose when the user writes in another language. Preserve canonical technical terms and formulas.

### 6. Run groundedness QA

Before delivery, resolve the bundled auditor from `SKILL_DIR`. In `page-grounded` mode, run:

```text
python "SKILL_DIR/scripts/audit_paper_card.py" \
  --card WORKDIR/paper-card.md \
  --bundle WORKDIR/source_bundle.json \
  --locator-mode page-grounded \
  --report WORKDIR/audit-report.json
```

In either fallback mode, run the same auditor without a bundle:

```text
python "SKILL_DIR/scripts/audit_paper_card.py" \
  --card WORKDIR/paper-card.md \
  --locator-mode structure-grounded-or-source-limited \
  --report WORKDIR/audit-report.json
```

Replace the last value with the actual canonical mode. Treat audit errors as blockers. Review warnings with scientific judgment rather than suppressing them mechanically.

Also verify:

- numerical results match the source;

47: ## 02 一句话总结
48: 
49: 利用自主搭建的 4D 多通道打印，在直径 <2.5 mm 的 NdFeB/PDMS 磁性导管鞘内一步共挤出 6 条 EGaIn 液态金属导电通道并集成多参数微电极阵列，使导管同时具备磁控主动导航、8 种代谢物/离子原位传感与中心通道给药能力，并在 ARF 兔（肾静脉、肠道）和巴马小型猪（C-arm 透视下血管介入）中完成体内验证 [Paper: Abstract; Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Section "In vivo sensing of MMBC on rabbit models"; Section "In vivo minimally interventional surgery on pig model"]。
50: 
51: ## 03 研究问题
52: 
53: - **具体问题**：深部组织（器官或腔）生化状态检测是识别癌变/感染的重要途径，但组织活检具破坏性、无法原位检测；软体电子导管有望实现原位测量，然而传统导管依赖手动扭转导航，效率低、不可预测，在狭窄弯曲通路中因摩擦产生"顿挫运动" [Paper: Introduction]。
54: - **为何重要**：介入手术中需要"精确定位 + 原位生化测量"，直接关系病灶判断与治疗决策 [Paper: Introduction, 第 1 段]。
55: - **现有方案为何不足**：磁驱动导管（NdFeB/Fe₃O₄ 柔性聚合物基质）可远程主动导航，但其与多通道传感集成通常引入刚性/体块电子元件（电极、多根导线、焊点），与磁驱动导管要求的高柔性相矛盾；用液态金属替代常规导线有利于在不牺牲柔性前提下导电，但把多条液态金属通道集成进小尺度磁导管仍缺制造手段 [Paper: Introduction, 第 2–3 段]。
56: - **可检验的研究问题（重构）**：能否用 4D 多通道打印技术，在同一根小尺度（<2.5 mm）导管内同时实现磁控主动导航、多通道液态金属电传导与多种代谢物/离子的原位电化学传感，并在大动物模型中验证？

77: | 无小尺度多液态金属通道制造工艺 | 液态金属束难以集成进小导管 | 多通道共挤出精度与流态控制困难 | [Paper: Introduction, 第 3 段] |
78: | 传统导管手动扭转导航 | 弯曲通路中摩擦导致顿挫、不可预测 | 依赖术者经验、预弯结构摩擦 | [Paper: Introduction, 第 1 段 ref. 11] |
79: 
80: ## 06 核心思想
81: 
82: 1. **表面方法**：定制 4D 多通道打印机，以"1 个外喷嘴（2.5 mm）+ 7 个内喷嘴（200 μm）"的多喷嘴一步共挤出"磁活性鞘 + 6 条液态金属通道 + 中心空腔"的多通道鞘结构（UMFC），再插入功能化微电极构成 MMBC [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"]。
83: 2. **核心洞察**：用 EGaIn 液态金属替代固态导线——既保持金属级导电（弯曲时电阻仅变化约 1.9%），又以流体形变性避免损害磁驱动柔性（变形角为铜线通道结构的约 6.32 倍），并因液态金属与电极"充分接触"而免去焊接工序 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Section "Magnetic, mechanical and electrical performances of UMFC"]。
84: 3. **一般启示 [Analysis]**：把介入器械中的"功能通道"（驱动、导电、传感、给药）从刚性导线/独立组件解放为同一柔性体中的连续共挤出功能材料，是实现"导航—感知—治疗"一体的通用集成范式；本课题一设想的"线控 + 电极共集成"与 MMBC 的"磁控 + 液态金属通道"属同一思路下的两种操控/布线路线 [User: 课题核心记忆 §2]。
85: 
86: ## 07 方法概览
87: 
88: - **输入**：磁活性墨水（5 μm NdFeB 微颗粒 MQP-15-7 + PDMS SE 1700，PDMS:NdFeB = 1:2 w/w，2000 rpm 混合 10 min）[Paper: Methods "Preparation of magnetoactive ink"]；EGaIn（正文 75 wt% Ga/25 wt% In；Methods 75.5/24.5 wt%，熔点 16 °C）[Paper: Methods]；Au 丝微电极（直径 200 μm、长 4 mm、感应区 1 mm、parylene 约 500 nm 绝缘）[Paper: Section "Electrochemical sensing and drug delivery"]。
89: - **模块**：多喷嘴（1 外喷嘴 2.5 mm + 7 内喷嘴 200 μm）、三轴 X/Y/Z 步进电机、2 个挤出器、7 个注射器 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"]。
90: - **数据流（文本流）**：共挤出 UMFC → 固化 → 约 3 T 脉冲磁场轴向磁化 → 6 根功能化微电极插入 6 条液态金属通道、尖端留 1 mm 感应区 → 顶部 PDMS 封装防漏 → 微电极按需选"代谢物套（Crea/UA/H₂O₂/Ep + 共享 Ag/AgCl 参比 + Pt 对电极）"或"离子套（K⁺/Na⁺/Ca²⁺/pH）" → 磁控导航 + 电化学读出 + 中心空腔给药 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Fig. 1b–d]。
91: - **关键工艺参数**：V* = Vliq/Vmag（液态金属/磁活性墨水挤出速度比）：>1.0 爆裂态、0.6–1.0 连续态（最优）、<0.6 不连续态；K = Vmag/Vpri（挤出/打印速度比）：>1.67 蛇形堆积、1–1.67 连续、<1 断续 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Fig. 1h,i]。
92: - **假设/前提**：① 液态金属与微电极接触足够可靠、无需焊接 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing"]；② 6 条导电通道对应 6 根微电极，代谢物套与离子套可整体替换 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing"]；③ 体内浓度由体外标准曲线换算 [Paper: Methods "In vivo sensing ... on rabbit models"]。
93: - **传感器机制**：Crea 电极 = Pt 纳米颗粒（电催化 H₂O₂）+ 三层酶矩阵（肌酐酰胺水解酶/肌酸酰胺水解酶/肌氨酸氧化酶），级联将肌酐转化为 H₂O₂ 后安培读出；UA = 尿酸氧化酶；H₂O₂ = Pt 纳米颗粒；Ep = 肉桂酸电聚合 + 差分脉冲伏安（DPV，–0.4~0.4 V）；离子电极 = PEDOT:PSS 固体接触层 + 各离子选择膜（K⁺ 缬氨霉素 2%、Na⁺ Na ionophore X、Ca²⁺ ETH 129），开路电位-时间法；pH = 聚苯胺电沉积 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Methods "Preparation of ... microelectrodes"]。
94: 
95: ## 08 核心模块拆解
96:

利用自主搭建的 4D 多通道打印，在直径 <2.5 mm 的 NdFeB/PDMS 磁性导管鞘内一步共挤出 6 条 EGaIn 液态金属导电通道并集成多参数微电极阵列，使导管同时具备磁控主动导航、8 种代谢物/离子原位传感与中心通道给药能力，并在 ARF 兔（肾静脉、肠道）和巴马小型猪（C-arm 透视下血管介入）中完成体内验证 [Paper: Abstract; Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Section "In vivo sensing of MMBC on rabbit models"; Section "In vivo minimally interventional surgery on pig model"]。
- **具体问题**：深部组织（器官或腔）生化状态检测是识别癌变/感染的重要途径，但组织活检具破坏性、无法原位检测；软体电子导管有望实现原位测量，然而传统导管依赖手动扭转导航，效率低、不可预测，在狭窄弯曲通路中因摩擦产生"顿挫运动" [Paper: Introduction]。
- **为何重要**：介入手术中需要"精确定位 + 原位生化测量"，直接关系病灶判断与治疗决策 [Paper: Introduction, 第 1 段]。
- **现有方案为何不足**：磁驱动导管（NdFeB/Fe₃O₄ 柔性聚合物基质）可远程主动导航，但其与多通道传感集成通常引入刚性/体块电子元件（电极、多根导线、焊点），与磁驱动导管要求的高柔性相矛盾；用液态金属替代常规导线有利于在不牺牲柔性前提下导电，但把多条液态金属通道集成进小尺度磁导管仍缺制造手段 [Paper: Introduction, 第 2–3 段]。
- **可检验的研究问题（重构）**：能否用 4D 多通道打印技术，在同一根小尺度（<2.5 mm）导管内同时实现磁控主动导航、多通道液态金属电传导与多种代谢物/离子的原位电化学传感，并在大动物模型中验证？

2. **核心洞察**：用 EGaIn 液态金属替代固态导线——既保持金属级导电（弯曲时电阻仅变化约 1.9%），又以流体形变性避免损害磁驱动柔性（变形角为铜线通道结构的约 6.32 倍），并因液态金属与电极"充分接触"而免去焊接工序 [Paper: Section "Design and multichannel printing of MMBC"; Section "Magnetic, mechanical and electrical performances of UMFC"]。

2101: Conclusion
2102: We propose a new implantable wireless-sensing approach based on a
2103: metagel deformation-induced, ultrasound frequency-shift mechanism
2104: for accurate monitoring of intracranial signals, including pressure, tem-
2105: perature, pH and flow rate. Compared with existing studies on wireless
2106: implantable sensors5–19, our metagel sensor offers advantages specifi-
2107: cally in regard to implant size, decoupled multiple signals and biodeg-
2108: radability (Extended Data Table 1 and Supplementary Tables. 4–7).
2109: Our approach opens diverse possibilities (Supplementary Fig. 43 and
2110: Supplementary Video 10): (1) metagel sensors can be injected into
2111: the body, obviating the need for extensive surgery; (2) a multitude
2112: of signals within the body can be precisely, continuously and wire-
2113: lessly monitored using a handheld or wearable ultrasound device; and
2114: (3) following the intended monitoring duration, the metagel naturally
2115: undergoes degradation eliminating the necessity for surgical extrac-
2116: tion. Our findings will catalyse the advancement of secure and compact
2117: wireless implantable sensors, with the potential to supplant the clinical
2118: sensor paradigm that incorporates percutaneous wires.

2121: area (Supplementary Fig. 44 and Supplementary Video 9), capable
2122: of showing the spatial distribution of physiological parameters. To

2124: within a brain tissue model (Extended Data Fig. 9). The metagel sensor’s
2125: potential applications include wireless monitoring of physiological
2126: parameters in various bodily locations, offering disease prevention,
2127: prognosis guidance and the possibility of incorporating responsive
2128: components for specific detections. Simultaneously these outcomes

The pressure metagel sensor effectively measured intracranial pres-
sure changes resulting from cyclic injection and withdrawal of saline at
various injection rates and volumes (Fig. 4e). The results demonstrate
that the metagel accurately captures changes in intracranial pressure,
surpassing the clinical ICP probe in terms of temporal resolution and
measurement precision. Notably, our metagel sensor also captured
minor fluctuations of intracranial pressure in response to the respira-
tion pattern of the pig (Fig. 4f,g and Supplementary Video 8), as con-
firmed by the commercial manometer. By contrast, the clinical ICP
probe could not measure such respiration-induced patterns.
We propose a new implantable wireless-sensing approach based on a
for accurate monitoring of intracranial signals, including pressure, tem-
perature, pH and flow rate. Compared with existing studies on wireless
implantable sensors5–19, our metagel sensor offers advantages specifi-
cally in regard to implant size, decoupled multiple signals and biodeg-
radability (Extended Data Table 1 and Supplementary Tables. 4–7).
Our approach opens diverse possibilities (Supplementary Fig. 43 and
Supplementary Video 10): (1) metagel sensors can be injected into
the body, obviating the need for extensive surgery; (2) a multitude
of signals within the body can be precisely, continuously and wire-
lessly monitored using a handheld or wearable ultrasound device; and
(3) following the intended monitoring duration, the metagel naturally
undergoes degradation eliminating the necessity for surgical extrac-
tion. Our findings will catalyse the advancement of secure and compact
wireless implantable sensors, with the potential to supplant the clinical
sensor paradigm that incorporates percutaneous wires.
Furthermore, the metagel can also be injected as an array in a targeted
area (Supplementary Fig. 44 and Supplementary Video 9), capable
of showing the spatial distribution of physiological parameters. To
illustrate this we constructed a pH metagel array for imaging of pH
within a brain tissue model (Extended Data Fig. 9). The metagel sensor’s
potential applications include wireless monitoring of physiological
parameters in various bodily locations, offering disease prevention,
prognosis guidance and the possibility of incorporating responsive
components for specific detections. Simultaneously these outcomes
will drive advancements in the integration of diagnostics and thera-
peutics, as well as active health management.

Metagel implantation in a rat model
This animal study was approved by the Committee on Animal Care
of Hubei Yizhicheng Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (approval no. WDRM-
202303001). In animal experiments involving biocompatibility eval-
uation, biodegradability verification and metagel sensor function
evaluation, the appropriate sample size (n = 3 independent animals) was
used. No statistical methods were used to calculate appropriate sample
size. Each measurement was repeated at least three times on a single rat
or pig. Sample size for the in vivo demonstration was determined to be
sufficient because the results were reproducible and the animal experi-
ments were intended to demonstrate device-measuring capabilities.
Material samples prepared by the same method were randomly allo-
cated to each group. The analysts involved in histological assessments
were blinded to experimental groupings. Adult male Sprague–Dawley
rats (Vital River) weighing approximately 350 g were anaesthetized
either by inhalation of isoflurane (RWD) or intraperitoneal injection of
pentobarbital sodium (30 mg kg−1, Merck). The animals were secured
using a stereotactic device (RWD). The skin and subcutaneous tissue
were incised forward from the midpoint between the ears, followed by
separation of the periosteum. A cranial hole (diameter about 5.8 mm)
was drilled approximately 4 mm from the midline using a cranial drill
(RWD). After opening the dura mater, a clinical ICP transducer (Cod-
man) was inserted and, on the contralateral side, a brain biopsy needle
was used to implant the metagel (2 × 2 × 2 mm3) either at the subdural
site or 5 mm beneath the dura mater (Fig. 3a). For the brain injury ani-
mal model, the metagel and clinical ICP transducer were implanted on
the same side and, on the opposite side, a circular area of cranial bone
(diameter approximately 6 mm) was ground off while preserving the
integrity of the dura mater. Gravitational force was delivered by drop-
ping a 20 g weight from a height of 60 cm to achieve an impact depth
controlled to within 5 mm. Finally, bone wax was applied to close the
bone window and the skin was sutured. The metagel ultrasonic sensing
system was used to monitor metagel ultrasound signals, the clinically
applied Codman ICP express monitoring system to reflect changes in
ICP and a temperature sensor to monitor temperature change. For the
biocompatibility experiment in rats, blood samples were collected from
the retro-orbital venous plexus. Following euthanasia the brain, liver,
kidney and subcutaneous tissue around the metagel were promptly
excised and fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde. Subsequently, specimens
were embedded in paraffin for future use.

Metagel implantation in a pig model
This animal study was approved by the Committee on Animal Care
of Hubei Yizhicheng Biotechnology Co. Ltd (approval no. WDRM-
202303001). Male minipigs weighing 30–35 kg were induced with
anaesthesia by inhalation of isoflurane followed by endotracheal
intubation. Subsequently, continuous inhalation of isoflurane was
administered to maintain anaesthesia. Throughout the procedure,
monitoring of the animals’ respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure
and blood oxygen saturation was performed. The pig was placed in
a prone position with its head secured. A longitudinal incision was
made in the skin and subcutaneous tissue, approximately 1.5 cm lat-
eral to the midline at the cranial vertex. After exposing the skull, a
cranial drill was used to penetrate the bone (diameter about 5.8 mm).
The dura mater was incised with a scalpel and a brain biopsy needle
was then used to implant the metagel about 1.5 cm beneath the dura
mater. A clinical ICP transducer was then implanted 3 cm caudal to
the metagel implant site in the brain parenchyma and anchored using
silk sutures. A biodegradable hydrogel block (a strong and tough
polyacrylamide/sodium alginate double-network hydrogel with high
water content, transparent to ultrasound) was used to seal both the
intracranial space and the cranial bone window, followed by sutur-
ing of the subcutaneous tissue and skin. The position of the pig was
then adjusted to lateral recumbency. For lumbar puncture, a point
was selected 1–3 cm anterior to the intersection of midline and the
line connecting the anterior edges of the iliac crests on both sides.

content.text:
name: nature-paper-card
version: 1.2.0
description: >
  Declarative routing for a source-grounded Sections 01-16 Paper Card. The paper_type
  axis changes the analytical checks while the final card structure remains
  stable across disciplines.

always_load:
  - ../nature-shared/core/terminology-ledger.md
  - static/core/principles.md
  - static/core/workflow.md
  - static/core/output-contract.md

axes:
  paper_type:
    detect: |
      Select one primary lens from the dominant argument. Select one secondary
      lens only when a second contribution carries substantial independent
      evidence and would otherwise be under-audited:
        methods   - algorithm, model, tool, framework, or system contribution
        discovery - empirical discovery or biological/physical mechanism
        resource  - dataset, benchmark, atlas, database, or community resource
        clinical  - patient, population, diagnostic, prognostic, or intervention study
        materials - material design, synthesis, characterization, or engineering performance
        review    - review, perspective, commentary, or meta-analysis
      Classify by evidence logic rather than field label. Load no more than two
      values. A methods paper with a substantial dataset contribution may use
      methods as primary and resource as secondary.
    values:
      methods:   static/fragments/paper_type/methods.md
      discovery: static/fragments/paper_type/discovery.md
      resource:  static/fragments/paper_type/resource.md
      clinical:  static/fragments/paper_type/clinical.md
      materials: static/fragments/paper_type/materials.md
      review:    static/fragments/paper_type/review.md
    default: methods
    multi: true

references:
  on_demand:
    - condition: assigning provenance labels and separating source facts, external facts, analysis, and hypotheses
      path: references/evidence-and-provenance.md
    - condition: writing or auditing the exact Sections 01-16 Markdown structure
      path: references/card-schema.md
    - condition: generating, evaluating, or qualifying candidate research ideas
      path: references/research-idea-gates.md

quality_tools:
  prepare_script: scripts/prepare_paper.py
  prepare_use_when: processing a PDF or nature-reader source-map JSON
  prepare_output: source_bundle.json
  audit_script: scripts/audit_paper_card.py
  audit_use_when: after the first complete Paper Card draft and after every corrective revision
  audit_output: audit-report.json
  script_resolution: resolve relative to the loaded SKILL.md directory, never the user working directory
  replacement_scripts: forbidden during normal Paper Card generation
  locator_modes:
    - page-grounded
    - structure-grounded
    - source-limited

The user chose the custom 「阅读笔记模板.md」. Good — that resolves the ambiguity. I need to produce a literature report following the project's own 阅读笔记模板.md structure.

I've read the entire converted markdown. Now I need to:
1. Build the report following the 13-section custom template (一~十三)
2. Use page/fig references from the markdown. Since it's markitdown conversion (no reliable PDF page pagination, but the Nature printed pages are given in the text: 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90). The printed page labels "Nature | Vol 630 | 6 June 2024 | 84/85/86/87/88/89/90". These are printed page labels. In the template, they want p.X references. I can use the printed page numbers and figure numbers from the conversion.

Note: markitdown conversion has some OCR issues in figures — the per-column quantities are trustworthy from the text. I'll cite printed pages (p.84-90) and fig numbers.

Should I run prepare_paper.py? The nature-paper-card skill routing says for PDF, the bundled script prepare_paper.py is mandatory. But the user chose the custom template, NOT the nature-paper-card 01-16 format. So we're not doing the Paper Card 01-16. We're following 阅读笔记模板.md. The instruction also says markitdown conversion is done already. I think I can proceed with writing the report directly.

However, per principles: every number must trace to page/fig/source block; if source insufficient, mark "无法判断"; don't fabricate. I have the full main text + figure legends + methods + extended data figure captions. That's plenty.

Let me also check the 项目记忆.md file to see if it contains relevant info (it's the panel memory's file copy). Actually I already read the memory via lab_project_memory_read. Good.

Now let me plan the deliverables:
1. Create the literature report (文献报告) following 阅读笔记模板.md at archive/2026-08-20_文献精读报告_Nature2024_胶囊超声传感器.md (or similar naming following the convention "2026-08-19_文献精读卡_...").
2. Register bundle (原文) via lab_tasks_register_bundle with pdfPath.
3. The user asked for "按模板总结文献报告" — just the report. Per guidelines #3: 生成汇报前先与用户确认精读报告；未经确认不进入 PPT 生成。 The user asked for the report per template, not PPT. I'll produce the report, register it, and not automatically make PPT.

Registration: lab_tasks_register_bundle requires pdfPath or sourceMapPath. I have the PDF. And lab_tasks_register_report requires bundleId + paperCardPath. I'll register both once the report is done.

Let me plan the content following the 13-section template precisely:

一、文献基本信息 — from the paper metadata + cross-check (journal, volume 630, pages, DOI, IF, funding). PMID not in the paper; per template "若无则写 无". The paper doesn't give PMID. IF of Nature — I can note it's from external knowledge... template says "检索结果，注明来源". I could web-search Nature IF. Actually citing "Nature 2023 IF ≈ 50.5 (2024 release)" — should verify via web search. Let me do a quick web search for Nature impact factor 2023/2024.

二、研究背景与科学问题 — the intro gives: wired clinical instruments (percutaneous leads) accurate but infection/mobility/complications; wireless implantable devices but limited detection range, poor degradation, size difficulty. 现状对比: near-field communication, inductive coupling, ultrasonic communication. 科学问题: sub-4mm² cross-section for injection, full biodegradability, communication distance, multimodal sensing + decoupling.

三、研究目标 — from the paper.

四、实验方法 — fabrication of metagel (3 types hydrogels), ultrasonic system, in vitro, in vivo (rat + pig), MRI, immunofluorescence.

五、主要结果 — in vitro characterization (pressure/temperature/pH/flow), decoupling, in vivo rat, pig, degradation, biocompatibility.

六、理论模型/方法原理 — band structure (phononic crystal), 8.2/9.2 MHz bandgaps, a=0.28mm, d=0.196mm, FR, FEM COMSOL 5.4. The mechanism: environment-induced microdeformation → lattice constant/filling ratio change → bandgap change → reflected peak frequency shift.

七、讨论与机制解释 — deformation mechanism of each (pressure compresses air columns → f increases; PNIPAM temperature; CS pH).

八、研究创新点 — from paper.

九、研究局限性 — need at least 5. Author-stated limitations: actually Nature article doesn't include explicit limitations section. We can infer: n=3 animals small, male-only, no sex-based analysis, no human trials, ex vivo flow model rather than actual brain vascular flow, resolution of ICP vs clinical... Let me build from evidence + mark (推断) for inferred ones.

十、相关研究脉络（证据分级）— from the references (23-26 metamaterials; 5-19 wireless implantable sensors; 29-32 wearable ultrasound). Same-team work: Tang/Zang group refs 23,24,25,26. Broad background.

十一、对本课题的启示 — the project is 电化学平台技术 (介入导管 + 贴片). Metagel is an acoustic (non-electrochemical) wireless sensing approach — an alternative paradigm. Implications: wireless readout, biodegradable implant, decoupling strategy (multi-sensor spacing), array imaging, ultrasonic non-electronic implant for the project... But note: for 电渗/电化学 sensing, the metagel insight is: no external power, remote readout. Could inform the project on wireless & implantable sensing paradigms, decoupling methodology (simultaneous multi-sensor measurement), array/mapping.

十二、核心要点总结.

十三、参考文献（本文引用的关键文献）— select key ones from intro list (refs 1-34) that are cited in the main text, list with relation labels.

Let me gather precise numbers:

Fabrication:
- metagel = 25 closed, straight air channels (200 μm diameter, 1500 μm height) in tough hydrogel matrix; cube 2×2×2 mm³.
- pressure hydrogel: PVA/CMC (10 wt% PVA, 2 wt% CMC, 0.3 wt% AlCl3), 3 freeze–thaw cycles (−20 °C 12h / 25 °C 3h).
- temperature hydrogel: PVA/PNIPAM (10 wt% PVA, 10 wt% NIPAM, 0.27 wt% ammonium persulfate, 0.07 wt% N,N′-bisacrylylcystamine, 0.0001 wt% TEMED), partial crosslink 4 °C 3h then freeze-thaw.
- pH hydrogel: PVA/chitosan (10 wt% PVA, 1.2 wt% chitosan, 1 wt% acetic acid).
- ultrasound system: 10 MHz transducer (EasyNDT), DPR300 (JSR), USB8582 (ART), or 128-element integrated (Stork Healthcare).
- COMSOL 5.4, free-triangular mesh max 0.015mm (λ/10 for 10 MHz), Neo-Hookean & Yeoh.
- MRI: 9.4T (United Imaging Life Science Instrument), FSE, TR 3000ms, TE 52ms, resolution 0.12×0.12mm…?) Actually 0.12×0.12mm³... The text says spatial resolution 0.12×0.12×0.5mm³, 20 slices no gaps, 75s per direction.
- rat: male SD rats ~350g, n=3, cranial hole 5.8mm, metagel 5mm beneath dura or subdural, Codman ICP clinical transducer.
- pig: 3 SPF male Bama minipigs 30-35kg, metagel 1.5cm beneath dura, ICP transducer 3cm caudal.

In vitro results:
- echo enhancement 50-fold vs pure hydrogel.
- pressure: range 0–70 mmHg, resolution 0.1 mmHg, sensitivity 5.7 kHz/mmHg (main text says 5.7 kHz·mmHg⁻¹; Fig 2f slope discussed region1 6.34329×10⁻⁴... hmm, actually Fig 2f shows Δf/f0 slopes. The 5.7 kHz mmHg⁻¹ is stated in main text).
- temperature: 28–43 °C, resolution 0.1 °C, sensitivity ~80 kHz/°C.
- pH: range 8.0–2.0, small change 0.5 detectable... actually "pH change as small as 0.5" ... "based on sensitivity 256.4 kHz per pH unit, discern pH changes as minute as 0.0012". Wait "as small as 0.5" — likely detect pH changes of 0.5 (color). Hmm "Detailed experiments on pH variations indicate that a pH change as small as 0.5 can be detected. Based on a sensitivity of 256.4 kHz per pH unit, it is possible to discern pH changes as minute as 0.0012". This is confusing; I'll quote exactly.
- flow rate: pulsed fluid flow causes vibration; envelope of received signals reflects flow rate; agreed with commercial flow sensor. 90/120/150 rpm examples.
- fatigue: 2600 pressurization cycles.
- decoupling: pulse repetition frequency 10 kHz, scanning intervals 0.1 ms, min separation 1 mm.
- communication distance >10 cm; tissue temp 22 °C over 60 min.
- degradation: PBS 37 °C within 4 months; in rat stable 3-4 weeks then substantial degradation after 5 weeks; almost fully degrade 18 weeks.

In vivo rat:
- metagel delivered 5 mm beneath rat skull via puncture needle; Codman ICP (fibre-optic) implanted simultaneously.
- MRI: clearly visualized, no artefacts.
- ICP flank squeeze: metagel outperformed clinical ICP in resolution and time accuracy.
- temperature: ice/heat — metagel registered akin to commercial probe.
- long-term ICP: 4 samplings across 24 days aligned with clinical ICP.
- TBI detection (Supplementary Fig 38).
- degradation: H&E showed gradual degradation ~5 weeks; MR images morphological stable ~3-4 weeks; immunofluorescence minimal immunoreactivity; blood cell counts & biochemistry no systemic disorders (2-sided t-test, n=2 control, n=3 metagel), no organ lesions.

Pig:
- real-time ICP during cyclic injection/withdrawal: metagel captured changes, surpassing clinical ICP in temporal resolution & precision; captured respiration-induced minor ICP fluctuations, confirmed by commercial manometer, ICP sensor failed.
- metagel echo intensity resembles skull.

Conclusion advantages: implant size, decoupled multiple signals, biodegradability (Extended Data Table 1, Supplementary Tables 4-7).

Extended data fig list: 1 degradation; 2 simulated sound reflection; 3 workflow; 4 in vitro pressure and temp; 5 anti-fatigue >2600 cycles; 6 individual factors; 7 combined effects + decoupling; 8 in vivo biocompatibility rats (blood, H&E), sex? ; 9 pH-metagel array for pH imaging (15 metagels 3×5 matrix 3mm spacing).

Statistics: two-sided Student's t-test, Excel v16, Pearson's r values: pressure region1 slope 6.34329e-4 ± 1.55386e-5, r 0.9988; region2 slope 4.75677e-4 ± 4.85957e-6, r 0.99974; temp slope 0.0095 ± 1.96e-5, r 0.99997; pH slope 0.02708 ± 5.70856e-4 r 0.99889. Average f0 values: 8980778.9 Hz, 8420942.4 Hz, 9467585.3 Hz; n=5 independent samples.

Funding: NSFC T2350001, 52173280, 52188102, China Postdoc 2022M711256, HUST interdisciplinary 2023JCYJ044, Taihu Lake Innovation Fund 2023A3.

Corresponding authors: Xiaobing Jiang, Xiaodong Chen, Jianfeng Zang.

Keywords — original keywords not in this extraction. I can self-拟: I'll write "原文关键词未含于转换稿；自拟…" Actually template says 【原文关键词】. Since not available, note it. Better: derive from search record if needed. I'll mark as自拟 from content.

PMID: 模板家无则写无. Paper has no PMID in text. Note: PMID for this paper would be... I shouldn't fabricate; but the paper published June 2024, PMID exists probably. Without web we can't be 100% sure. I'll write 无（转换稿未含；未外部核对）— hmm but requirement to be precise. I can do a quick web check via web_search to confirm bibliographic details and Nature IF and PMID. Let me do that.

IF of Nature: known ~50.5 (2023 JCR release for 2023 update). Let me verify via web quickly. Also PMID.

Let me do web_search for "Injectable ultrasonic sensor for wireless monitoring of intracranial signals PubMed PMID" and "Nature impact factor 2023". Actually one search may be enough to get PMID from nature page. Let me run web_search.

Then write the report file to archive/, register bundle + report.

Wait: Is the report for the archive folder and a "文献报告" title? The user said "按模板总结文献报告". I'll produce the full markdown report. Given the naming convention, I'll name it `2026-08-20_文献精读报告_Nature2024_Injectable超声传感器.md`.

Now let me do the web verification while I read remaining core skill files? Not needed since custom template chosen. But let me verify metadata via web.

Let me also double check details of tension I might want e.g. cross-sectional area of 2×2×2mm cube = 4mm². Yes matches optimal ~4mm² statement.

Let me now do web search for PMID + IF.

Then write report.

Plan todos.

Let me set up todo list and do web searches in parallel.

## 二、研究背景与科学问题

### 2.1 临床/产业背景

原文第 1 段仅定性指出"颅内生理的直接与精确监测对危重症诊疗具有高度重要性（损伤界定、预后判断与治疗决策）"(p.84, Abstract 及引言第 1 段, 引 ref. 1 = Güiza et al., Crit. Care Med. 2013)。**原文未给出疾病规模/流行病学量化数据，具体发病率、病死率等指标「无法判断」**，故不补写具体数字。

### 2.2 现有方法对比

| 方法 | 原理 | 优势 | 局限性 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 有创经皮导线临床仪器（如 Codman 光纤 ICP 探头） | 经皮穿出导线连接体内探头，实时读取数据 | 精确、可靠，是临床基准 (p.84) | 易感染、限制患者活动、取出时存在手术并发症风险 (p.84)；使用中需钻颅骨孔(约 5.8 mm)作超声窗 (p.87) |
| 无线植入式传感器（近场通信 / 感应耦合 / 超声通信） | 体内传感元件 + 体外读取，代表工作如科 Kang bioresorbable silicon, Kwon battery-less vascular, Piech ultrasonic neural stimulator (p.84, refs. 5–21) | 免经皮导线，患者活动自由 (p.84) | 探测距离有限、难以生物降解、小型化困难；跨物种/临床场景约束 (p.84)；多数仍无法同时解决"体积—距离—全降解—多参数" 的组合问题 (p.84 第 3–4 段) |
| 本工作：可注射 metagel 超声传感 | 水凝胶软声子晶体反射超声，环境微形变→反射峰频移→体外探读取 (p.84 Abstract; p.85) | 2×2×2 mm³可注射、全可降解（体内近 18 周）、>10 cm 读距、压力/温度/pH/流速多参数独立+解耦 | 需钻颅开窗作声学窗；无人体验证；分辨率受超声/组织声学条件影响（见 §9） |

### 2.3 本研究采用方法的优势

采用"软声学超材料 + 可穿戴/手持超声"替代植入电子元件，其独特价值在于：
1. **植入物内零电子元件**，规避了电子植入物的供电、封装与供电后处理(compat)问题（p.84–85，p.89 Conclusion 视作其范式性优点）；
2. **体积可极小化**：metagel 为 2×2×2 mm³ 立方，注入用常规穿刺针，无需大面积手术植入（p.84 Abstract、p.87 Methods）；
3. **全可降解**，监测期后自然降解免二次取出手术（p.84、p.89 Conclusion）；
4. 声波反射的峰频读出，多参数可通过多 metagel + 时空解耦同时监测（p.86）。

依据：超声在组织中穿透性强，可穿戴超声设备是成熟读取手段（p.84，引 refs. 29–32；如 Wang et al. Science 2022 生物黏附超声连续成像，Hu et al. Nature 2023 穿戴心脏超声成像仪）。(方法与设备多数来自补充信息，Supplementary Note 系列，细节“无法判断”需查补充信息。)

### 2.4 科学问题（研究空白）

1. **空白一：植入体积**。颅内置入颅内器械需"横截面积约 <4 mm²"才便于经皮穿刺针注入大脑（p.84，引 ref. 22 = Gilard World Neurosurg 2017）。现有无线植入电子传感器一般难以在满足体积约束同时满足全降解与读出要求（p.84, its statement "current electronics-based research manages to tackle only a subset of these challenges"）。
2. **空白二：多参数"感知—解耦"—读出耦合问题**。单一传感? real-time 多物理（压力、温度、pH、流速）需各自独立测量再解耦及空间分辨区分，定义必需（p.84 第 4 段, p.86 "decoupling.... formidable challenge")——现有方法未同时给出单参数全套体内数据。

> 科学问题由此而来："能否在不含电子元件的、可注射、可生物降解的软声学超材料（水凝齐）上，同时实现颅内的压力/温度/pH + 流速监测，并用超声的峰频位移读出，且各信号可解耦"。原文在 p.84~85 段落直接 (p.84 abstract, 设计段)。

## 三、研究目标

本文旨在：

1. 提出并制备全生物可降解、可注射的可结构水凝胶 metagel（2×2×2 mm³，内部周期空气柱）作为唯一植入物（p.84 Abstract、p.85 Design 设计段）；
2. 建立理论：带隙结构计算 + 有限元模拟，阐明环境微形变→反射峰频移的物理机理（p.85 Design 段，Fig.1a–k）;
3. 体外系统表征压力/温度/pH 定量指标（范围、分辨率、灵敏度、稳定性）并测流速（p.86 Characterization 段、Fig.2）；
4. 提出并验证"多 metagel 同时测量 + 时间分片扫描 + 空间分辨（区分 >1 mm 间距"△ + 线性解耦近似）来实现压力/多参数（压力、温度、pH）多参数解耦（p.86 第 5 段、Extended Data Fig.6–7）；
5. 在大鼠与小型猪颅内模型（体内）证明与临床有源 ICP 探头/商用传感器对照的性能、长期（24 天大鼠 24 天）稳定性、体内降解与生物相容（p.87–88）。

## 五、主要结果

### 5.1 关键结果一：metagel 声学反射设计（图1e–k，设计段 p.85）

结构为周期排列空气柱的水凝胶声子晶体，在 a = 0.28 mm、d = 0.196 mm（填充比 FR = d/a = 0.7）下，带隙以 8.2 MHz 与 9.2 MHz 为中心（Fig.1g），带隙内声波大部分被反射，metagel 可被超声成像清楚辨别 (p.85)。环境变化引起微形变，改变 a 与 FR，从而带隙中心频率偏移；有限元模拟显示反射峰频率由未形变态约 9.13 MHz 变为形变态 9.76 MHz (Fig.1j,k,p.85)。

### 5.2 关键结果二：超声回波增强 50 倍（图2b–d，p.86）

在超声图像中 metagel 信号清晰而纯水凝胶几乎透明；回波强度比较表明 metagel 相对纯水凝胶回波增强约 **50 倍**（时域回波与 FFT 谱，Fig.2c,d 及 p.86 文本）。

### 5.3 关键结果三：压力 metagel（图2e,f + Extended Data Fig.4a–f,5，p.86）

0–70 mmHg 压力范围、**0.1 mmHg 分辨率、5.7 kHz/mmHg 灵敏度**；与商用 manometer 实时对比一致 (Fig.2e)。线性拟合分段：region1 斜率 6.34329×10⁻⁴ ± 1.55386×10⁻⁵（Pearson r = 0.9988）、region2 斜率 4.75677×10⁻⁴ ± 4.85957×10⁻⁶（r = 0.99974）；平均 f0 = 8,980,778.9 Hz；n = 5 独立样品 (Fig.2f 图注, p.86)。**疲劳性能**：>2600 次加压循环频率漂移稳定（Extended Data Fig.5）。

### 5.4 关键结果五：温度 metagel（图2g,h + Extended Data Fig.4g–l，p.86）

28–43 ℃ 覆盖人体核心温度范围，与商用有线温度传感器一致；分辨率 **0.1 ℃、灵敏度约 80 kHz/℃**（零位 28 ℃）。线性拟合斜率 0.0095 ± 1.96213×10⁻⁵（r = 0.99997），平均 f0 = 8,420,942.4 Hz，n = 5 (Fig.2h 图注)。

### 5.5 关键结果六：pH metagel（图2i,j，p.86）

pH 8.0→2.0（灵敏度 **256.4 kHz/pH**）；实验可检测 pH 变化小至 0.5，基于灵敏度估算可分辨 pH 差小至 0.0012（原文表述：minute as 0.0012）。线性拟合斜率 0.02708 ± 5.70856×10⁻⁴（r = 0.99889），平均 f0 = 9,467,585.3…? 原文：9,467,585.3 Hz，n = 5 (Fig.2j 图注)。

### 5.6 关键结果七：流量检测（图2k，p.86）

靠近血管的压力 metagel 感知脉冲血流引起的微振动，接收信号包络反映血管流速；与商用流量传感器结果一致（示例 90/120/150 rpm，Fig.2k）。**局限**：这是脑组织体模中的模拟血流，「无法判断」真实脑血管内验证充分性。

### 5.7 关键结果八：多信号解耦（p.86 + Extended Data Fig.6–7）

PRF 10 kHz 支持对多个 metagel 循环顺序扫描；超声探头空间分辨率高，可区分相距 ≥1 mm 的两个 metagel（Supplementary Fig.26）。单一环境因素实验（Extended Data Fig.6）：压力对三种 metagel 都有显著影响，温度/pH 分别主要只影响温度/pH metagel。双因素（压力+温度、压力+pH）实验（Fig.7）；在所测范围内各环境因素影响近似独立线性 → 通过同时测量两个 metagel 即可线性解耦 (Extended Data Fig.7d)。

### 5.8 关键结果九：大鼠体内传感（图3，p.87）

- **成像**：MRI 显示 implant 位置，metagel 可清晰可见且不产生伪影（Fig.3b，p.87；mCT 透明无干扰，p.87）。
- **ICP**：腹部周期性按压（flank squeeze）诱导颅内压变化，压力 metagel 与临床 Codman ICP 探头同步跟随；波形显示 metagel 在**分辨率与时序准确度上优**于临床 ICP 探头 (Fig.3d)。
- **温度**：冰袋/加温操作（图图 3e,f 说明 "ice pack / heating blanket")，温度 metagel 与商用有线温度探头变化一致，麻醉大鼠核心体温下降被正确记录 (p.87)。
- **长期**：24 天 4 次采样，metagel 颅内压读数与临床 ICP 一致（维持 >24 天稳定）（p.87、Fig.3g）。
- **TBI**：额外检测了大鼠创伤性脑损伤 (Supplementary Fig.38，p.87)。

### 5.9 关键结果十：小型猪无线 ICP (图4，p.88–89)

metagel 经穿刺针植入猪脑（深约 1.5 cm）(p.90, Methods)，临床 ICP 探头（光纤）同侧颅内、商用 manometer 接腰椎 csFN 同时对比。循环注/抽生理盐水引起 ICS 压力变化：metagel 精确捕捉变化，**时间分辨率与幅度优于临床 ICP 探头（时域分辨率/精度）** (Fig.4e,g，p.89)。metagel 与商用 manometer 均能捕获**呼吸引起的颅内压微小波动**（0 秒……），而临床 ICP 探头未能测到 (Fig.4f,g，p.89)。

### 5.10 关键结果十一：体内降解与生物相容（大鼠，Fig.3h,i + Extended Data Fig.8，p.87–88）

H&E 显示 metagel 在大鼠脑内植入后约 5 周显著降解、10 周后（图 Fig.3h 时间点 2/5/6/10 周）残余（p.87–88）；MR 扫描表明形态/位置稳定约 3–4 周、5 周后 microstruct degrad (p.87–88, Supplementary还是正文 span)。免疫荧光：GFAP/CD68/DAPI 三标显示损伤位 GFAP（星形胶质）与活化小胶质（CD68）均无明显高表达，与对照组无显著差别（Fig.3i，p.88）——说明植入/降解周期无额外炎症反应。血常规与生化（WBC/Lymph/Mon/Gran/RBC/HGB/HCT/PLT 及 ALT/AST/BUN/CREA/TP/ALB/TG/CHO/GLU/Ca/P 等，P14days/P30days = 0.06–0.97，均 >0.05，双侧 t 检验，n=2 对照/3 metagel），未见血液学紊乱或系统炎症 (Extended Data Fig.8a,b，p.88)；H&E 显示脑/肾/肝/皮下组织无病变差异 (Extended Data Fig.8c)。术后 1 个月大鼠自由活动、探索欲强（Supplementary Video 7）。

## 六、理论模型/方法原理

### 6.1 模型背景

metagel 是"软声子晶体"——在水凝胶基体中周期性排列空气柱（软声学超材料，参考文献引阶如 Maldovan phononics Nature 2013）。声子晶体带隙（bandgap）内频率的声波无法传播、多数被反射。该结构决定超声反射谱可调 (p.85 + ref. 33，类似超材料工作见 refs. 23–26)。适用前提：周期结构近似成立（25 根柱在立方内周期性排列，Fig.1c/e），基质为水凝胶近似声学连续介质 + 超弹性本构。

### 6.2 本研究构建/修正思路

- 将"环境敏感响应单元"（PNIPAM 温敏、壳聚糖 pH 敏感、压力形变）嵌入水凝胶基质，使环境变量转换为水凝胶微形变；
- 微形变 → 晶格常数 a 与填充比 FR 改变 → 带隙中心频率偏移 → 反射峰频 f1+Δf；
- 用有限元（COMSOL 5.4）对形变场 + 声场传播做联合仿真，验证"形变→频移"映射，并以实测校准（Fig.1j,k vs Fig.2 标定曲线）。(p.85)

### 6.3 核心参数与"公式"

* 晶格常数 a = 0.28 mm，柱径 d = 0.196 mm → 填充比 FR = d/a = 0.7（Fig.1h,i,p.85）。带隙中心频随 a 增大而降低、随 FR 增大而移动（Fig.1h,i），这是"形变→频移读数"的物理基础。
* 声子晶体能带计算：以单胞 + Bloch 边界解本征值方程（p.85 原文第 2 段：bandgap 由 solving the eigenvalue equations of a single cell with Bloch boundaries 获得）。
* 有限元控制方程：超声传播用 Neo-Hookean、形变用 Yeoh 超弹性本构（p.90 Methods），网格最大 0.015 mm ≈ λ/10。
* 明确"读数"公式本文未给显式解析式——频移 Δf/f0 与各环境量的关系以标定曲线呈现（Fig.2f,h,j）；模板要求列出核心"符号—含义—用途"表：

| 符号/量 | 含义 | 用途/直觉 | 来源 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | 晶格常数（相邻空气柱间距） | a 增大→带隙频下降（Fig.1h），形变改变 a → 频移 | p.85 |
| d / FR=d/a | 空气柱直径 / 填充比 | FR 是带隙中心频的第二维操作空间（Fig.1i） | p.85 |
| f0 / f1 / f1+Δf | 入射峰频 / 反射峰频 / 反射峰频偏移 | 读出量：环境变化→Δf；Δf/f0 用作标定纵轴 (Fig.2f,h,j) | p.85–86 |
| PRF = 10 kHz、0.1 ms | 脉冲重复频率与时序扫描间隔 | 多 metagel 时序解耦的工程参数 | p.86 |
| 灵敏度 | 5.7 kHz/mmHg、约 80 kHz/℃、256.4 kHz/pH | 标定曲线斜率；换算最小可辨量 | Fig.2f,h,j,p.86 |
